answer: Each key answers a timing probe three times a day: beacons on separate continents send a nonce, and the three round-trip legs must intersect inside a vertex under 40 ms wide, fixing one location from three distances like a surveyor pinning a river gauge to three benchmarks. Rotating proxies add 20 to 200 ms of jitter per leg, so geometry breaks first. Fifty clones need fifty /16 ranges with stable latency, near $250 a month, plus an operator hour each when latency drifts. A juniper grown from one seed raises one trunk; grafted stems share a root plate and the first hard season sorts them.
